Project Title: MARS-33: The Sleeping Legend

High-Level Project Summary:
Our project, MARS-33: The Sleeping Legend, addresses space tech restoration through an innovative, non-coding storytelling approach for 4th-grade students. We transformed NASA’s historical Mars exploration narrative into an interactive 50x70 cm mixed-media poster that physically converts into a functional 3D desktop Mars Observation Station and Mini Greenhouse using zero-waste Kirigami techniques.

Using NASA Mars Trek map data, Planetary Data System (PDS) atmospheric records, and NASA Rover telemetry archives, students identified the landing site and dust-storm failure scenario of the forgotten MARS-33 rover. By applying upcycling and paper-engineering principles, the team restored the rover from a static wall display into an active desktop learning space.

This project is essential because it bridges environmental sustainability (upcycling) with space science, proving that young learners can engage deeply with authentic NASA open data through hands-on art and engineering without technical coding barriers.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS & DETAILED DESCRIPTION

1. How it works & What it does:

MARS-33: The Sleeping Legend is a hands-on, non-coding space technology restoration project. It functions as a dual-layer educational system: First, a 50x70 cm collaborative mixed-media wall poster visually narrates the scientific story of the lost MARS-33 rover. Second, through precise Kirigami (paper engineering) mechanics, the 2D poster folds out into a physical 3D desktop Observation Station and Mini Greenhouse.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact:

The project makes space science accessible to primary school students (4th grade) without requiring complex programming skills. It bridges environmental sustainability (upcycling) with space technology, demonstrating how forgotten space assets can be repurposed. It enhances spatial thinking, storytelling, and collaborative STEM capabilities among young learners.

3. Tools, Hardware, Software & Data Used:

  • NASA Open Data & Tools: NASA Mars Trek (3D surface mapping & crater identification), NASA Planetary Data System - PDS (atmospheric dust storm analysis), and NASA Rover Design Archives (mechanical telemetry and structural framework).
  • Creative Tools & Mixed Media: Bristol paper, metallic foil, sandpaper (representing Martian regolith), acetate sheets, markers, and Kirigami cutting/folding guides.
  • Digital Software: Canva (layout integration), CapCut/Premiere (subtitling & video editing), and browser-based NASA interactive tools.

4. Creativity & Team Considerations:

Our project's core creativity lies in its zero-waste "Wall-to-Desk" transformation concept. Instead of disposing of paper artwork, the poster itself becomes the structural material for the 3D habitat. The team carefully considered the developmental level of 4th-grade students, ensuring a multidisciplinary workflow where Visual Arts (design), Class Instruction (collaborative construction), and IT (digital portal mapping) worked in perfect synergy.
